findings.text: The `command:<name>` event used to be emitted on the command itself. It is now emitted only on `this.parent`, and only when a parent exists. A listener like `cmd.on('command:' + cmd.name(), ...)` is never called. This also applies to a root program with an action handler, because `this.parent` is undefined there.

The new `else if (this.parent && this.parent.listenerCount(commandEvent))` branch runs before the operands, `*` and unknown-command handling. If a command has no action handler but its parent has a `command:<name>` listener, that listener fires and the rest is skipped. Example: `prog.on('command:sub', ...)` with `sub` having subcommands, then running `prog sub bogus`. The unknown-subcommand error and the `command:*` fallback never run, and `sub`'s own help or error handling is bypassed.

0.reason: This finding describes the same root cause as the reference bug: the command:<name> event is now emitted on the parent (or not at all for root) instead of on the command itself, masking the intended event dispatch.

1.reason: This is a distinct defect where the new parent-listener branch bypasses operand, wildcard, and unknown-command handling, causing incorrect behavior when a parent has a command:<name> listener but the subcommand lacks an action handler.
